steps.title: Superlative adjectives
steps.html:
The adjectiveRuleExample
short (old, high)the + -estthe oldest, the highest
one vowel + consonant (big, hot)double + -estthe biggest, the hottest
ends in -y (busy, easy)-y → -iestthe busiest, the easiest
long (beautiful, expensive)the most + adjectivethe most beautiful
irregular—good → the best, bad → the worst

A superlative almost always has the in front of it.

After it we usually say in a place or of a group: the highest mountain in Africa.

one of the most… + a plural noun: one of the largest volcanoes in the world.

Learners often write the most biggest. Use -est or the most, never both.

steps.title: Four records, four surprises
steps.html:
The driest place. Not the Sahara. The driest place on Earth is a valley in Antarctica, where it hasn't rained for two million years. It is also one of the coldest places in the world.

The oldest restaurant. Sobrino de Botín in Madrid opened in 1725 and it is still open today. It is not the most expensive restaurant in the city, and it isn't the biggest — it is simply the oldest.

The busiest airport. Atlanta in the USA is busier than any airport in Europe or Asia, but most of its passengers never leave the building: they only change planes there.

The strangest one. The shortest war in history was in 1896. It was between Britain and Zanzibar, and it was over in thirty-eight minutes.
